mechanism: Binary session_overlap=1 when ≥2 of Sydney/Tokyo/London/NY UTC sessions are active; plus per-session 20-bar rolling std of log returns masked to that session, forward-filled and shift(1) to avoid lookahead—conditions the model on institutional participation windows.
data_needed: DatetimeIndex (UTC), close prices; session UTC hour bounds; rolling std on session-masked returns.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex majors (EURUSD H1 example); M1–H1/D1 with frequency gate; UTC session clock.
why_new_for_mis: MIS can sense liquidity/volatility regime as joint session-overlap state plus lagged within-session realised vol, not a single global ATR.
quote: The most important temporal feature for intraday trading models is not any individual session flag but the session_overlap indicator: a binary flag that is 1 whenever two or more sessions are simultaneously active.

mechanism: Encode hour/dow/doy as sin/cos on unit circle; expand hour to k=1..n_terms harmonics so the feature set can represent bimodal/trimodal forex activity (Asian peak, London open, LN–NY overlap) that a single harmonic cannot.
data_needed: Bar DatetimeIndex; n_terms (default 3); timeframe gate for which features get extra harmonics.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex; minute bars get multi-harmonic hour; H1+ use base harmonic only.
why_new_for_mis: Clock topology as a regime embedding—MIS senses where in the multi-peak trading day the bar sits without discrete hour integers.
quote: Representing the bimodal London–New York structure requires at least a second harmonic (k = 2). The third harmonic (k = 3) captures three-peak patterns such as the Tokyo–London–New York session rhythm.

mechanism: Discrete flags friday_ny_close (Fri hour≥21), sunday_open (Sun hour≤2), month_end (day≥28), quarter_end (month%3==0 & day≥28) mark predictable rebalancing/gap windows; frequency-gated to daily+ bars.
data_needed: Day-of-week, day-of-month, month, UTC hour from index.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex; D1/W1/MN1 retain calendar flags; intraday drops them.
why_new_for_mis: MIS calendar-flow sensor for period-boundary liquidity/pressure regimes distinct from price-path features.
quote: Days 28–31 of the calendar month concentrate institutional rebalancing flows. Fixed-income portfolio managers rebalance duration, equity funds match their benchmark weights, and FX desks execute associated currency hedges.

mechanism: For non-time bars (volume/dollar/tick), bar_duration=seconds between bar timestamps and bar_duration_accel=Δduration; shorter/accelerating bars sense rising market urgency vs slow formation.
data_needed: Alternative-bar timestamps; is_time_bar=false path in CTimeFeatures.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol; volume/dollar/tick bars (MQL5 CTimeFeatures); EURUSD M15/H1 verification context.
why_new_for_mis: Formation-speed sensor of information arrival rate when clock time is not the bar clock—MIS activity-change without raw tick count alone.
quote: A dollar bar that forms in 45 seconds carries very different information about market urgency than one that takes 4 hours.

mechanism: Roll: effective spread from √(−Cov(Δp_t,Δp_{t−1})) when cov<0 else NaN; Corwin-Schultz from adjacent high-low pairs yielding cs_spread and Beckers-Parkinson cs_sigma (bid-ask-adjusted intraday vol).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic EURUSD-like bars; FX sub-daily noted for more NaN alphas; OHLCV or tick-augmented.
why_new_for_mis: OHLCV-only liquidity and noise-adjusted vol sensors—MIS spread/impact state without L2 quotes.
quote: The cs_sigma column returned by corwin_schultz_spread() is therefore the Beckers-Parkinson volatility as a byproduct of the spread model. It is a bid-ask-adjusted intraday volatility estimate.

mechanism: Rolling OLS: Kyle λ = slope Δp on signed volume (tick rule); Amihud ILLIQ = mean |log ret|/(close·volume); Hasbrouck λ on signed √dollar volume; Kyle/Hasbrouck also emit t-stats to discount thin-window estimates.
data_needed: Close, volume; optional precomputed tick directions b_t; window≈20.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic EURUSD-like; equity/FX tick or OHLCV proxy.
why_new_for_mis: Triple price-impact / illiquidity sensor suite with reliability t-stats—MIS adverse-selection intensity beyond spread width.
quote: A high Kyle's Lambda means that a given quantity of buy volume moves the price by a large amount, implying that market makers suspect informed trading and widen their quotes.

mechanism: Partition ticks into equal-volume buckets; VPIN = mean |V^B−V^S|/V* over n buckets; high VPIN = one-sided informed flow; used as regime variable with lambdas/entropy, not standalone Flash-Crash oracle.
data_needed: Tick volume and mid/close; bucket_size, n_buckets (default 50); forward-fill to bars.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Tick stream joined to OHLCV bars; synthetic EURUSD-like demo.
why_new_for_mis: Volume-time order-flow toxicity regime for MIS—syncs sensing to traded volume rather than clock bars.
quote: Its value in an ML pipeline is therefore not as a standalone signal but as a regime variable: high VPIN indicates order flow imbalance, which the model can combine with the lambda estimates and entropy features to characterise the current microstructural regime.

mechanism: Build micro feature matrix X; label MM profit/loss via triple-barrier; fit classifier; map OOS cross-entropy loss through KDE CDF to φ_τ∈(0,1)—high φ = predictable adverse-selection environment, low φ = informed-trader regime (Flash-Crash lesson).
data_needed: Micro features (VPIN, λ, cancellations…); triple-barrier labels; rolling classifier + KDE on −L_t.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AFML Ch.19 framework; equity MM / Flash Crash narrative; CPCV pipeline link.
why_new_for_mis: Meta-regime sensor of how predictable the MM problem is—MIS senses information asymmetry via model loss, not raw imbalance alone.
quote: The result φτ ∈ (0, 1) measures how predictable the market maker's environment is at time τ.

mechanism: Rolling first-order autocorrelation of signed volume proxies large-order splitting persistence (complements VPIN magnitude); bar_microstructure_features add tick/volume/dollar imbalance and buy_fraction from ticks inside each bar.
data_needed: Tick stream with prices/volumes; bar boundaries via searchsorted; signed volume series.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: LSE stocks literature (Tóth); general tick+OHLCV bars; E-mini round-lot notes.
why_new_for_mis: Persistence-of-imbalance and per-bar signed-flow sensors—MIS detects worked institutional inventory, not just contemporaneous toxicity.
quote: A feature measuring the first-order autocorrelation of signed volume in a rolling window is therefore a proxy for the presence of a large order being worked in the market.

mechanism: On MT5, CopyTickVolume is price-change counts not trades; bar-close tick rule × tick volume feeds Kyle/Hasbrouck—treat λ as ordinal regime (rising impact) not cardinal impact; Roll/CS remain broker-comparable.

instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5 viewer example; any MT5 symbol/period with OHLCV.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit sensing policy for retail FX feeds: liquidity-impact features as regime ranks when true trade tape is absent.
quote: The practical consequence is that the lambda values produced by the MQL5 implementation should be treated as ordinal regime signals rather than cardinal price-impact estimates.

mechanism: Encode intrabar tick rule {−1,0,+1}→message; Shannon H (marginal concentration), plug-in Hw (w-gram structure), Lempel-Ziv c(n)/n (compressibility), Kontoyiannis match-length entropy rate—low H/LZ on trends, high on random; all four jointly disambiguate oscillating vs trending regimes.
data_needed: Per-bar tick-rule sequences; word_length; Konto window; uint8 encoding.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic bars with random/trend/oscillate regimes (~24 ticks/bar); AFML Ch.18.
why_new_for_mis: Order-flow information-content regime sensors—MIS senses informed/directional concentration and sequential predictability inside the bar.
quote: Low entropy is therefore a signal that the order flow within the bar is directionally concentrated, which the microstructure literature associates with informed trading.

mechanism: CSW supremum standardized log-price departure vs time-dependent critical value (excess = stat−crit); SADF = sup ADF t-stat over backward-expanding starts on log prices—map β<0 steady (mean-reversion), β≈0 unit-root (reduce size), β>0 explosive (trend)—as continuous features plus optional three-way discretisation.
data_needed: Log prices; min_length τ; optional rolling L; CSW one/two-sided; SADF model/lags/phi.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic EURUSD-like 300 bars with injected explosions; daily/hourly research series.
why_new_for_mis: Formal real-time regime-change sensors that select strategy family—MIS change detection beyond heuristic MA crossovers.
quote: Structural breaks, the transition from one market regime to another, represent some of the best risk-adjusted trading opportunities precisely because most participants are caught off guard.

mechanism: QADF replaces SADF supremum with high quantile Q_{t,q} of inner ADF dist plus tail width Qdot; CADF = conditional mean C_{t,q} above quantile; outlier_ratio=(SADF−C)/c_dot flags when supremum is a single singular window, not broad explosiveness.
data_needed: Same log-price ADF grid as SADF; q≈0.95, v≈0.025.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AFML Ch.17; synthetic bubble series shared with SADF demos.
why_new_for_mis: Robust bubble/regime-change sensors plus a diagnostic that MIS can use to distrust spurious SADF spikes.
quote: when SADF rises far above C_{t,q}, it signals that the supremum is being driven by an outlier window rather than by a broad explosive trend in the inner distribution.

mechanism: EA-side SADF uses fixed lookback L (default 252) so each update answers 'explosive in last L bars?' at O(L²) cost; pairs with CSW excess, Chow break-bar, SM-Exp/SM-Power trajectory shape for live strategy routing.
data_needed: Log closes via CopyClose; min_length, lookback L; thresholds sadf_explosive/steady.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 validation; H1 with L scaled down; any MT5 symbol/period.
why_new_for_mis: Current-window explosiveness regime for live MIS—distinct from expanding-window 'ever bubbled' historical max.
quote: The rolling window changes the interpretation of SADF in one precise way: it answers "is the series explosive within the last L bars?" rather than "has it ever been explosive?".

mechanism: EMD decomposes series into IMFs + residue; omit finest Reconstruction harmonics and sum remaining splines, extrapolating a few bars—senses dominant oscillatory modes vs noise; strict mode uses only real extrema (EMD.mqh) vs loose future-extremum balance (EMDloose).
data_needed: Open (or selected) price window Length; Forecast depth; Reconstruction count; CEMD.decomp.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 (Length≈110–250, Forecast 2–4 recommended); TestEMD EA 2018–2020.
why_new_for_mis: Adaptive mode sensor of the price path’s intrinsic oscillations—MIS short-horizon structure without fixed Fourier basis.
quote: after having obtained the IMF functions, we can sum up some (but not all) of them and obtain a smoothed version of the initial series. It is the smoothed reconstruction that will act as the source of forecasting.
